note: Laws in force on 1 January 2000; these are gameplay classifications. Economy: market economy after 1990s privatisation with a large state share. Trade: moderate tariffs and selective protection. Conscription: universal male service. Press: major national broadcasters under state or state-majority ownership alongside privately owned outlets. Elections: competitive multi-party elections (the CPRF won the most Duma seats in 1999) in which administrative and media rules favoured incumbents. Civil rights: limited by the military operation in Chechnya. Religion: secular constitution with no state church. Immigration: managed, with free movement from much of the former USSR. Internet: lawful intercept without national filtering. Healthcare: compulsory medical insurance funds.
